name: Japan
summary: Where Larry's service ended, as a patient. Flown out of Vietnam sick at the end of his tour, by way of Subic Bay in the Philippines, he came to the hospital at Camp Zama: "I was at Camp Zama in Japan in Sugami Uro." "I think close to 4 months," he says of his stay. His DD-214 gives his last duty assignment as a U.S. Army medical command in Japan. He made a friend there, the patient in the bed across from him, a man from back east whose name he no longer remembers, and on a pass they went to the Ginza together and found a German restaurant down a flight of stairs. Japan is also where he saw his own name on a list of the killed: "In the first 3-4 days I saw the name in the KIA list and went straight to the chaplin in the hospital in Camp Zama. I told him I was KIA and I was still alive."
researchNotes: Larry named the hospital unprompted (2026-08-13, giscus-stories-c18006833): told only that research had a high-confidence candidate, not which one, he wrote "Camp Zama in Japan in Sugami Uro" [read as Sagami-Ōno], converging with the documentary case: the U.S. Army hospital at Camp Zama / Sagami-Ōno was in Sept–Nov 1965 effectively the only Army hospital in Japan receiving Vietnam evacuees, and APO 96343 on the DD-214 is Camp Zama's. Full research note: research/places/japan-hospital-1965.md. His son's paraphrase of 2026-09-03 puts the arrival at about 3 September 1965 (2026-09-03-phone-camp-zama-date.json). The route: 2026-08-23 (giscus-stories-c18118868), "Flew first to the Philippines and spent 4 days at a navy base or navy hospital"; 2026-09-03 (giscus-stories-c18259364), "they flew me to Subic Bay in the Philippines and I was there 4-5 days", and in the paraphrase of the same day, Subic Bay Naval Hospital. The Philippines stop is Subic Bay in his account; corrected 2026-09-14 after research/site-audit-2026-09-14.md, where this note had suggested Clark AB. "Close to 4 months" from early September runs past the 30 November 1965 separation on the DD-214, so the duration is a soft estimate. Corrected 2026-09-14: this note said coordinates wait on Larry confirming the hospital; he named Camp Zama on 2026-08-13. No coordinates are set because this record is the country, not the hospital. Also corrected 2026-09-14: Captain Geutler was linked here; Larry has him flying Larry off the mountain at the start of the evacuation, not in Japan, and the family brief's KIA paraphrase that carried the link does not name him. Remaining goals: NPRC clinical records (filed by hospital name; research/records-request/); the German restaurant of the Ginza day (research/places/ginza-heidelberg.md); the hospital friend. The medical detail in the 2026-08-12 call notes (2026-call-japan-medevac.json) renders on this page when it returns; whether it should is a family decision.
